title: C (programming language)
summary: C is a general-purpose, imperative, procedural language created in 1972 by Dennis Ritchie. It provides programmers with relatively direct access to CPU architecture features, making it suitable for implementing operating system kernels, device drivers, and protocol stacks. C supports structured programming, static typing, and recursion, with a small keyword set and user-defined identifiers. It compiles to low-level code that maps efficiently to machine instructions while maintaining cross-platform portability. The language offers manual memory management via pointers, a static type system with implicit conversions, and preprocessor directives for macros and conditional compilation. Standard libraries supply I/O, string manipulation, and mathematical functions. Since 2000, C has typically ranked as the most or second-most popular language in the TIOBE index, used across platforms from supercomputers to microcontrollers.

mechanisms.title: Static typing and manual memory management
mechanisms.explanation: C enforces a static type system with weak enforcement and implicit conversions between primitive types. Manual memory management is achieved through pointers and dynamic allocation functions from the standard library, giving programmers direct control over computer memory.

mechanisms.title: Preprocessor and compilation model
mechanisms.explanation: C uses a preprocessor for macro definition, source-file inclusion, and conditional compilation. The language is designed to compile to low-level code that maps efficiently to machine instructions with minimal runtime support, enabling direct hardware access while maintaining portability across platforms.
